messages.author: 8130a890dccc32e2
messages.subject: Multinomial Probabilities Set to Zero
parts:
Hello all,

Recently, I've run into an issue that I haven't been able to resolve on one of our projects. We want to run a multinomial distribution over various community data where the individual communities have zeros where the species are absent. In other projects, I've just let this be estimated as very small numbers within the multinomial; however, in this circumstance we have data on the species present at the site at the sampling time so we want to distinguish between species known to occur at a location vs ones that are in the larger species pool. We do need all of the information on all of the species present in each community probability vector for next steps with the project. Essentially our code looks like this:

mod <- nimbleModel({
      for(i in N_community){ #loop for the different communities
            CommunityObs[i, 1:N_species]~dmulti(size=community_size[i], prob=Pr[i,1:N_species]) #defining community proportional abundance vector
            Pr[i,1:N_species] ~ ddirch(alpha=alpha.P[i,1:N_species]) #prior distibution (all alphas=1)
         }
      })

Currently I've tried two things to help approach this issue:
  1. Setting the initial values for Pr where species are not known to occur to zero so they cause an issue an are not estimated. This runs but as the chains are running it spits out many warnings.
  2. Indexing though the values that we want to estimate. This caused errors saying that the indexing needs to be in the a:b form, since the indexes were presented as a list.
Any advice you have on this subject would be greatly appreciated.

Matt

messages.author: f116cbe5c604c988
messages.subject: Re: Multinomial Probabilities Set to Zero
parts:
Matt, thanks for your question.  I admit upfront, I'm not entirely following your question, but I have a few thoughts and questions.

I don't think your approach (1) is what you want.  Warnings are generally not good, and just setting the initial values of various elements of Pr[] to zero probably won't accomplish anything, since (assuming Pr[] is undergoing sampling) these values will readily be replaced with non-zero values, and therefore it feels like nothing was accomplished.

I'm not entirely sure what you mean by (2) "indexing through the values we want to estimate".  Also, the errors you're getting from that are most likely indicative of a problem, so I don't suspect this is working for you.  Maybe you can send along the code you tried using for (2) the indexing approach, which will give a better understanding of what you're trying to accomplish?

Other questions that will help me understand:
- Are all elements of Pr[] meant to be estimated?  Or are you attempting to fix some of them at 0?
- Are all elements of CommunityObs[] observed?  That is, do you have fixed "data" values for all elements of the CommunityObs[] array?

Cheers,
Daniel
